description.narrative:
The use of Artificial Intelligence for surveillance, profiling and stifling activism is on the rise, creating a distressing environment that deepens existing inequalities, threatens activists, and silences dissent. This trend not only undermines the rights of individuals but also stifles the voices of those fighting for change. With the rise of the far right exploiting digital tools for harm,It’s vital to recognize the implications for freedom and democracy, including public discourse, especially during elections, shed light on the need for vigilance and action in defence of civil liberties. This project will empower 36 activists in the Netherlands and Spain to understand, expose, and counter the systemic harms that artificial intelligence (AI) poses to activism and civic space. We will achieve this through applied research, cross-border learning exchanges, and the co-creation of activist-led strategic, replicable solutions that enhance the resilience of activists against the weaponization of AI. The project will apply the feminist influencing basket of resources and e-motive learning methodology that will engage the activists through a research aided context analysisand solution finding. It also builds a track record for ONL’s Dutch and European programming on digital rights
Artificial Intelligence is a growing intersectional threat fueling climate misinformation, exacerbating harm in humanitarian settings, targets vulnerable communities like LGBTQ, colored, black, Muslim, migrants, refugees,and aids manipulation in discourse and elections. The project aligns with Oxfam Novib and Intermon’s agendas to strengthen civic space and Dutch/European programming with a digital rights lens. By enabling and collaborating with activists, it promotes transnational cooperation and innovative cross-border strategies. It pavesthe way for AI and environmental justice initiatives(CJ), enhances digital resilience in conflict zones (SAFE), and integrates a feminist and gender perspective(ER4A). The project enhances ONL's visibility on civic space and digital rights while complementing existing efforts through Activist Lab, feminist resources, AACJ, Masarouna, and Tipping Point. It will also utilize Power to Voices, asa safer platform for activists, to further organize

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Intermon is a member of Oxfam International, a confederation of 17 independent national organisations working in more than 90countries. Oxfam works on six goals that support the shared vision of a just world without poverty: help people claim their right to a better life; champion equal rights for women; saving lives, now and in the future; safeguard global food supplies; help people claim a fairer share of natural resources; and increase money for basic services. For 70 years, Oxfam has been running emergency responses, development projects and campaigning at the grass roots level to tackle poverty.
